subject: dplyr support  for Character classes in data frames

messages.author: 919a40c48da677f7
messages.subject: dplyr support  for Character classes in data frames
parts:
I have a data frame that was created from a SAS transport file (XPT) using read.xport from library('SASxport'). When I try to use filter from dplyr I get an error. I can fix this by removing all the character classess from the data frame but that is not an elegant solution. Is it possible to add a feature in dplyr that would handle the simple filter below without causing an error but without removing the classes in the data frames since the classes can be useful at times.

> str(dm)
'data.frame':	5 obs. of  3 variables:
 $ USUBJID:Classes 'labelled', 'character'  atomic [1:5] 01-701-1015 01-701-1023 01-701-1028 01-701-1033 ...
  .. ..- attr(*, "label")= chr "Unique Subject Identifier"
 $ SEX    :Classes 'labelled', 'character'  atomic [1:5] F M M M ...
  .. ..- attr(*, "label")= chr "Sex"
 $ RACE   :Classes 'labelled', 'character'  atomic [1:5] WHITE WHITE WHITE WHITE ...
  .. ..- attr(*, "label")= chr "Race"
 - attr(*, "label")= chr " "
 - attr(*, "SAStype")= chr " "
> 
> dm <-select(dm,USUBJID,SEX,RACE)
> dm <-dm[1:5,]
> 
> dm[dm$SEX=="M",]
      USUBJID SEX  RACE
2 01-701-1023   M WHITE
3 01-701-1028   M WHITE
4 01-701-1033   M WHITE
> 
> filter(dm, SEX=="M")
Error: column 'USUBJID' has unsupported type

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d

Hadley,

I can only get it to work if I use unclass() in function metafix below. The metafix2 function below gives me the same error.

metafix <- function(ds) {
  ds[] <- as.data.frame(lapply(ds, function(x) {
  attr(x, 'SASformat') <- NULL
  attr(x, 'label') <- NULL
  x <-unclass(x)
  x}))
}

metafix2 <- function(ds) {
  ds[] <- as.data.frame(lapply(ds, function(x) {
    attr(x, 'SASformat') <- NULL
    attr(x, 'label') <- NULL
    attr(x, 'SAStype') <- NULL
    x}))

}

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: dplyr support for Character classes in data frames
parts:
Well, technically class is an attribute ;) You can simplify your code
a little to this:

metafix <- function(df) {
df[] <- lapply(df, function(x) {
attributes(x) <- list()
x
})
df
}

Hadley
